Executive Order 5930. October 6, 1932
Executive Order
AMENDMENT OF SCHEDULE A , SUBDIVISION VII, OF THE CIVIL-SERVICE
RULES
Schedule A of the civil -service rules , Subdivision VII, Post Office Department ,
positions excepted from examination under the civil -service rules , is hereby amended
by the addition of the following paragraph , to be numbered 6 :
6. Temporary clerks , carriers , and laborers required for part-time or intermittent
work in the Postal Service in connection with the present holiday or seasonal business
from this date to February 1, 1933 .
THE WHITE HOUSE ,
HERBERT HOOVER
October 6, 1932.
[No. 5930]

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The lead only adds paragraph 6 to Schedule A, Subdivision VII, of the civil-service rules; its whole content is that paragraph, which runs "from this date to February 1, 1933 .", so the lead ended with it by the order's own terms on 1933-02-01 (inclusive reading; exclusive reading ends it when that day begins). No earlier revocation or supersession was found.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 5930 (Herbert Hoover, October 6, 1932; register and WPA agree on the date and on Schedule A, Subdivision VII, Post Office Department, paragraph 6) is held in the Hoover Public Papers volume II OFR compilation (government printed copy, graded official compilation). Its text has two parts: an operative lead amending Schedule A and a single paragraph 6. Paragraph 6 limits itself to the present holiday or seasonal business "from this date to February 1, 1933 .", so the order ended by its own terms on that date. The date is recorded inclusive (the order runs through February 1, 1933); the exclusive reading, under which it ends when February 1 begins, is the alternative a reviewer should see. No later order, statute or rule extended it: the packet's number lookup over 33,118 held texts finds no other text citing Executive Order 5930, and the three machine searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, Federal Register catalog 1937 onward) record no hit; the catalog search cannot see anything before 1937, so the pre-1937 period rests on the held-text number lookup alone.
